advances: Repair of one prescribed three-fiber boundary martingale. It gives literal closed-halfspace credit and a single actual middle capacity. Different triples sharing a target need a separate joint capacity bound, and supporting allocations need their own implication.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write the old martingale as $\nu(ds)P_s(dt)$ with $s=(u_s,z_s,x_s)$ and use conditional probability rows on a full source set. A row at an extreme base can send only to the same base since its target base mean is that extreme. A base-zero row has equal masses $q(s)$ in its two endpoint branches, with $0\le q(s)\le 1/2$. Its mean in the direction $u_s$ is $h_{K_0}(u_s)$. All targets have the same normal, so the support heights in that mean identity give
$$
 q(s)\bigl(2h_{K_0}(u_s)-h_{K_-}(u_s)-h_{K_+}(u_s)\bigr)=0.
$$
Hence every positive crossflow row has tight support height, up to null sets. Each paired midpoint of endpoint targets lies in the actual middle support face by midpoint inclusion and the height identity. For $q(s)>0$, multiplying the prescribed probability pairing by $q(s)$ gives the row tuple measure. The two integrated tuple marginals are exactly $\gamma_-,\gamma_+$, each dominated by its physical endpoint surface measure. Their normal marginals agree because the original rows preserve the normal and the branch masses agree. Replacing the endpoint branches of each middle row by twice its paired midpoint branch preserves its total mass and physical mean. The retained base-zero branch feeds all of $\eta_0$, since endpoint-source rows cannot target base zero. This yields a normal-preserving martingale from $\nu_0=\nu|_{\{z=0\}}$ to $\eta_0+2\rho_{\rm old}$, so Jensen's inequality gives $\nu_{0,u}\preceq_{\rm cx}\eta_{0,u}+2\rho_{{\rm old},u}$ for $\lambda$-almost every $u$. For simultaneous conditional comparisons one can first apply Jensen to a countable determining family of convex tests on the compact physical support and then take uniform limits.

Disintegrate all these measures relative to $\lambda$ in their physical coordinates. Their normal marginals are dominated by $\lambda$ since the old martingale preserves the normal, its target has normal marginal $\lambda$, and each tuple branch has a mass equal to an endpoint crossflow. Thus the disintegrations are Borel kernels of uniformly bounded mass with fixed compact physical supports, after choosing versions on a common Borel full set. The two endpoint kernels have equal mass there, are dominated by the corresponding actual surface kernels, and vanish off the tight normal set. Write $\mu_{-,u},\mu_{0,u},\mu_{+,u}$ for the conditional surface kernels in the continuous coordinates. By the convex-surface normal disintegration, each such kernel of positive mass is equivalent to intrinsic Hausdorff measure on the corresponding full exposed face: it is the normalized conditional probability multiplied by the Radon–Nikodym derivative of that body's normal marginal with respect to $\lambda$.

At a good tight normal where the crossflow mass is positive, the two endpoint surface kernels are nonzero. The conditional all-ball inequality gives that the middle surface kernel is nonzero and supplies the ball inequality with $r=d-1$. Actual midpoint inclusion of the exposed faces follows from body inclusion and tightness. The face-alignment and density lemma therefore applies. If the common dimension is zero, the three faces are singletons with the middle point the endpoint midpoint. Choose small balls centered at the two endpoint points in the ball inequality. Their masses are the full endpoint atom masses, so their power mean, at least their minimum, is at most the middle atom mass. The crossflow mass is at most this minimum and the old midpoint law already obeys the ceiling.

For common dimension $m\ge1$, choose orthonormal tangent coordinates in the three parallel affine hulls, with the midpoint of the endpoint origins as middle origin. The midpoint of the two coordinate vectors is the actual midpoint in the middle chart. The endpoints have the finite positive ball densities on the Borel good sets of the alignment lemma. Each endpoint density can be replaced by zero off its good set, giving a finite nonnegative Borel representative of the same measure density: Lebesgue differentiation holds almost everywhere and the usual density is zero almost everywhere on the remainder. The good sets have full crossflow mass. The middle upper density agrees almost everywhere with the actual conditional surface density and has finite integral. It satisfies the required reciprocal-power inequality for every pair from the two good sets. The variable-density barycentric theorem with singleton bases, weights $1/2,1/2$ and dimension $m$ therefore gives a same-marginal coupling whose midpoint dominates the prescribed old law in convex order and is dominated by $\mu_{0,u}$. Finite convex functions of the physical coordinates restrict to finite convex tests on this chart, including the fixed physical base-zero coordinate at output. Zero crossflow is handled by the zero tuple measure.

The pointwise feasibility just proved is in the original physical coordinates. Apply the Borel density-controlled barycentric kernel theorem with parameter $u$, reference $\lambda$, old midpoint kernel, endpoint crossflow kernels, and actual middle surface kernel as the ceiling. It supplies a single Borel tuple kernel $\pi_u$ whose midpoint law $\rho_u$ has the desired conditional order and ceiling. In particular $\rho=\lambda(du)\rho_u$ on the middle bundle satisfies $\rho\le\eta_0$.

Apply the Borel tagged martingale reconstruction to $\nu_{0,u}$, $\eta_{0,u}$, $\rho_{{\rm old},u}$ and $\pi_u$, using the two conditional convex orders above. Its proof uses a martingale to $\eta_{0,u}+2\rho_u$, then splits the $2\rho_u$ branch by a Borel disintegration of $\pi_u$ over its physical midpoint, and chooses the two endpoints with probability $1/2$ each. Before this last choice the same tuple draw is a pairing of the two branches in each new source row. In fact the tuple branch has integrated mass $2\lambda(du)\pi_u$ before the endpoint choice, so the paired law using the mass of one endpoint branch is exactly $\lambda(du)\pi_u$. Keep the old endpoint-source rows. Their target marginals are the original residuals $\eta_z-\gamma_z$, so the full target is still $\eta$. The construction preserves the source law, the physical conditional mean and the normal. For each tuple, if its physical midpoint lies in $H$, at least one endpoint lies in $H$ by the defining affine inequality. Integration gives the asserted comparison for all closed halfspaces with that same tuple law.
statement:
Let $K_-,K_0,K_+$ be convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, attached to physical bases $-1,0,1$ and satisfying $(K_-+K_+)/2\subset K_0$. The marked bundle records $(u,z,x)$ with $x$ in the exposed face of $K_z$ at $u$. Let $\eta_z$ be the ordinary surface measure of $K_z$ on this bundle, marked by its almost everywhere unique outer normal. Put $\eta=\sum_z\eta_z$ and $\lambda=(u)_\#\eta$. Suppose a finite source measure $\nu$ on the same bundle admits a normal-preserving martingale to $\eta$ in the physical coordinates $(z,x)$. Let $\gamma_-,\gamma_+$ be the two target crossflows from base-zero sources to the respective endpoint bases.

For the given martingale, pair its two endpoint branches conditionally at each base-zero source using any Borel conditional pairing. Let $\rho_{\rm old}$ be the resulting marked midpoint measure, using the mass of one endpoint branch. There is a replacement normal-preserving martingale with the same source $\nu$ and target $\eta$, the same endpoint-source rows and the same two physical crossflow measures. It admits a single pairing of its new two endpoint branches with a marked midpoint law $\rho\le\eta_0$. Relative to $\lambda$, for almost every $u$ the physical conditional laws satisfy $\rho_{{\rm old},u}\preceq_{\rm cx}\rho_u$. If $H$ is any closed halfspace in the physical coordinates, the same pairing gives
$$
\rho(\{(u,0,x):(0,x)\in H\})\ \le\
\sum_{z\in\{-1,1\}}\gamma_z(\{(u,z,x):(z,x)\in H\}).
$$
title: Actual three-fiber surface midpoint repair with preserved crossflows
